No console errors related to routing. Did NOT re-run POST /api/product-slugs/generate (per review-request instruction — LLM cost/time).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_product_by_slug uses $or on {slug, legacy_slug} as the first lookup — clean and O(1). Good choice.

server.py get_product_by_slug also keeps case-insensitive regex + name-based fallback + 25-char prefix truncation fallback for very old URLs. This is 3 safety nets — comprehensive backward compat, but if the collection grows large, the fallback scan (to_list on category and full catalog) could be slow. Consider adding an index on {slug: 1} and {legacy_slug: 1} if not already present.

ProductCard.getProductUrl correctly prefers product.slug (short_slug, no brand) over deriving from name, and always emits /{category}/{brand}/{slug} when both brand+slug are available. Fallback chain (slug-only 2-seg, then model_number 2-seg, then /product/{id}) is sensible.

Breadcrumbs.generateBreadcrumbs.product uses product.short_title || product.name — this correctly picks the short SEO title when present. Brand link URL is /{catSlug}/{brandSlug} which matches the brand-filtered category fallback in the router. Consistent.

The brand-filtered page at /washing-machine/bosch renders 'Bosch Washing Machine - Buy Online at Best Price' with 28 products — verified working. This is served by the /:category/:brand route falling through to a brand-filtered category listing when the second segment doesn't match a valid model/slug in the 3-seg lookup.

short_slug_migration.py exposes POST /generate + GET /status under /api/product-slugs. Status endpoint returns state='completed'. No auth guard on POST /generate — consider adding admin-only guard because it triggers LLM cost (~7 min).

Consider adding a 301 redirect from legacy 2-segment URLs to the new 3-segment format for SEO consolidation (currently they resolve with 200 which is fine functionally but google will index both URLs).
